insights.title: Wheat futures rally amid collapsing export inspections
insights.description: Wheat futures prices surged 13.3% in five trading days (Oct 28–Nov 1) while weekly export inspections dropped 28.2% in W44 after a 34.2% decline in W43. The divergence suggests speculative buying or supply concerns (e.g., weather, crop damage) rather than demand-driven fundamentals. Root cause likely supply-side fears (e.g., drought, frost) or financial speculation, not actual export demand.
insights.root_cause: Supply-side fears (e.g., weather, crop damage) or speculative buying overriding weak demand signals from export data.
insights.forward_implication: If export inspections continue to fall while prices rise, a correction is likely when supply fears prove unfounded or demand weakness becomes apparent, potentially triggering a sharp price decline.
insights.metric_impact: 13.3% price increase on 97.6% volume surge vs 28.2% decline in export inspections; potential for $2-3/bushel correction if fundamentals reassert.

temporal_signals.change_description: Decreased 34.2% in W43 and further 28.2% in W44.
